doc.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Declaring the battle a tie, and the Basie party
summary: She wrote it up as a tie, then threw a party for the Basie band arriving in New York.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I think I wrote it up in Down Beat and I said it was a tie, and I was afraid that the musicians there would doubt it. But it went over as a tie you know. And after that, so that went very well, and built Chick, and he went into the Paramount Hotel and so on and so on. He was desperately ill all the time, but he used to faint after. He played five shows at the Paramount a day, and he would faint. He was — loss of blood and everything. But he was so game. So after that, you know, we said what’s next. And I don’t think they were too happy, but Basie came to town. And I’d been listening to Basie and Basie, they were very kind, Basie and Prez, and Bas’ said, “This gal is the gal that’s writing in Down Beat.” And Irving said to me, “I’ll let you give a party. I’ve got their recordings use. Ask everybody you want.” So as to everybody I could think of that meant something, that could play, and the New York Rhythm Club came in on it too, Milt Gabler and so on, and the Basie band came in. They didn’t play. Earl played and I’m not sure that Earl played, he was there. But anyway.
Are you talking about Earle Warren?

No Earl Hines. There’s only one Earl. But anyway it was a great success, it was wonderful. And so I knew that I really fell in love with the Basie band, because that was THE band, and THE rhythm section, and Lester. And of course the brass.
